# Technical subject

> **Scope:** System boundary covered by this explanation.
>
> **Reader:** Intended user, maintainer, or developer.
>
> **Source owner:** Link to the script, manifest, or pinned source map that owns
> code-dependent identity.

## Result or model

Lead with the durable conclusion or model. Separate storage identity from
event identity, intended input from actual artifact, or other distinctions that
prevent a plausible wrong interpretation.

## Mechanism and interfaces

Explain the components, ownership transitions, invariants, and failure modes.
Use dates and commits as provenance fields, not as the outline.

## Evidence basis

| Field | Record |
|-------|--------|
| Identity | Exercised board, source, package, kernel, configuration, or artifact. |
| Method | Command, workload, inspection route, or canonical reproducer. |
| Signal | Decisive pass or fail observation. |
| Trust | `MEASURED`, `CODE-INSPECTED`, `SOURCE-CONFIRMED`, `INFERRED`, or `UNVERIFIED`. |
| Reconstruction | Retained artifact or portable route to rebuild the evidence. |

## Boundary and rejected interpretations

State what the evidence does not establish and why likely alternative readings
are wrong or still unverified.

## Operations and current state

Link the canonical runbook or test for action, the project front door for
orientation, and status for the moving public verdict. Do not duplicate their
commands, backlog, or publication state.
